chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Set me upon the limits of faith.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and the acknowledgement of what he brought from Allah, and the five prayers, and the payment of zakat, and fasting the month of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to the House, and the Wilayah of our Wali and the enmity of our enemies, and entering with the truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What are the complete pillars of faith in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Abu Abdillah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi expands the traditional five pillars of Islam by integrating 'Wilayah' (authority of the Imams) and 'Ala' al-Adaw' (enmity of their enemies) as essential components of Iman, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of belief and allegiance. It underscores the doctrinal concept of 'Al-Dukhul ma'a al-Sadiqin' (entering with the truthful), linking personal piety to the cosmic hierarchy of the Ahl al-Bayt. This holistic view positions the Imam not merely as a political leader but as the spiritual axis of faith required for the validity of ritual worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Ajlan Abu Salih who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Set me upon the limits of the ‘Emān’ (faith). So heasws said: ‘The testimony that there is no god except for Allahazwj and that Muhammadsaww is Rasoolsaww of Allahazwj, and the acknowledgement with whatever hesaww came with from the Presence of Allahazwj, and the five Salāt, and payment of the Zakāt, and Fasting the Month of Ramazan, and Hajj of the House (Kabah), and the Wilayah for usasws and enmity for ourasws enemies, and the entering to be with the truthful’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ’Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from ’Ajlan ibn Salih who has said the following:

“I requested abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Teach me, please, the principles of beliefs. The Imam said, ‘They are: to testify and affirm that there is no one who deserves to be worshipped except Allah, to testify and affirm that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and to affirm that whatever he has taught is from Allah. (It is of the principles of beliefs) to affirm and accept that there is prayer five times every day. (It is of the principles of beliefs) to pay Zakat (charity), to fast in the month of Ramadan and to perform Hajj of the House (of Allah). (It is of the principles of beliefs) to love those who love us ( A ’immah from the family of the Messenger of Allah), to disown our enemies and to become part of the group of the truthful ones. (All such issues are of principles and obligatory matters).”’
